children: Our Bureau New Delhi: AceVector, the parent of ecommerce firm Snapdeal and listed software company Unicommerce, has reduced the size of its initial public offering, according to its draft prospectus filed on Monday. AceVector now plans to raise 287 crore in fresh capital, reducing from 300 crore earlier.

It has also pared the offer for sale (OFS) component by 35%. The OFS will see investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and Foxconn trim their holdings. The company is expected to announce the IPO price band Tuesday. Founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, who hold a combined around 34% stake directly and through related entities, won't sell their holdings in the IPO. The public issue will open for subscription September 25 and close September 29. The IPO anchor book will open September 24. IIFL Securities, CLSA and Systematix Group are the merchant bankers to the issue.

title: Snapdeal Parent AceVector Cuts its IPO Size in Draft Prospectus
